caseStudy.title: Guxo Flights
caseStudy.cardDesc: Booking an Ethiopian domestic flight on a phone, from search to boarding pass, with local payment options.
caseStudy.subtitle: A phone-first prototype for booking domestic flights across Ethiopia: search, compare fares, pick a seat, pay by phone and board.

shots.alt: Search screen: From, To, date and passengers
Results with fare comparison and the date strip

caseStudy.overview:
Guxo Flights is a working prototype of a domestic flight booking app for Ethiopia, built as a single self-contained web page with no frameworks.

It covers the whole trip: sign up, search between 10 domestic airports, compare fares, choose a fare and a seat, pay with local options, and manage trips through check-in and the boarding pass.

process.intro: Designed and built as one continuous prototype, so every screen could be tried on a real phone rather than only viewed.
steps: Mapped the booking journey end to end: search, results, fare and seat, payment, confirmation, trips and boarding.
Designed the search and results first, the screens travellers spend the most time comparing on.
Added the choices that matter locally: phone-wallet and bank-counter payment alongside cards, and prices in birr.
Built trip management after booking: My Trips, check-in, the boarding pass, notifications and a points programme.
Tuned it for phones first, with light and dark themes and layouts that also work on larger screens.

caseStudy.problem:
Booking a domestic flight on a phone often means dense results, unclear fare differences and checkout forms that ask for everything at once.

Many travellers also want to pay with a phone wallet or at a bank counter rather than only by card.

personas.intro: Proto-personas used to shape the flow (illustrative, not real people).

items.name: The business traveller
items.summary: Books at short notice and wants the fastest option without reading every row.
goals: Book in a couple of minutes

items.name: The family visitor
items.summary: Compares prices across dates and pays from a phone wallet.
goals: Find an affordable day to fly

items.name: The first-time flyer
items.summary: Is unsure what each fare includes and what happens at the airport.
needs: A boarding pass on the phone
goals: Arrive at the gate with confidence

caseStudy.insight: Travellers decide on the results and fare screens; if the differences there are plain (fastest, cheapest, what each fare includes), the rest of checkout can stay short.

ia.intro: Four tabs at the bottom; booking runs as one path from search to confirmation.

flow.title: User flow: from search to boarding pass
flow.intro: Captured from the working app after every change, so it always matches the current version.

caseStudy.solution:
A results list that labels the fastest and cheapest flights, shows fares across nearby dates, and lets travellers filter by stops and time.

Three clear fares (Basic, Standard, Flex) with what each includes, then a seat map, on one screen.

Checkout with phone, bank-counter and card payment, a single final price, and points earned shown up front.

After booking: My Trips, check-in and a boarding pass with a QR code, all on the phone.
caseStudy.outcome:
A complete, clickable booking prototype that can be tried on any phone, from sign-up to the boarding pass.

Covers 10 Ethiopian domestic airports, one-way and round trips, three fare types, a seat map, three payment methods, trip management and a points programme, with light and dark themes.

Its screenshots are taken automatically from the live app after every change, so this case study always shows the current design.
